PullRequest.Title: Editor: refine connected document tabs and high-contrast document wells
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Connected document tabs make the selected tab and editor read as one surface, with a distinct background for inactive tabs. Refs #331104.

## Design

- **Tab and background:** the selected tab uses `editor.background`; the inactive strip and tabs share `editorGroupHeader.tabsBackground`. There are no gaps between tabs, so adjacent hover begins at the selected tab's edge. Inactive labels use `tab.inactiveForeground`, with explicit theme customizations preserved.
- **Edges and border:** the first tab is flush with the document's left boundary; the final tab retains its curved shoulder. High-contrast themes outline the selected tab and document as one well, using `focusBorder` for the active group and `contrastBorder` for inactive groups. Normal themes reserve the same geometry with a transparent stroke.
- **Wrapped and pinned rows:** only the bottom row connects to the document. Upper wrapped rows and separate pinned rows use pills; selected tabs keep the document background on every row. Row fills stay equal at 28px default / 24px compact.
- **Text truncation:** tabs retain natural Fit sizing. Under compression, the filename keeps its first basename character, ellipsis, and extension, with space reserved for badges and actions. Extensions are protected only when the title matches the resource filename; arbitrary dotted titles remain fully ellipsizable. The full name remains available in the hover and ARIA label.
- **Icon-slot collapse:** file icons and their slots yield space before filename identity is lost, and return when the editor widens. Explicit compact pinned tabs retain their icon-only behavior.
- **Actions and scrolling:** selected close actions and dirty indicators remain visible; clean inactive close actions appear on hover or keyboard focus. Automatic reveal reserves both shoulders and the selected action, while first tabs and row starts stay flush. Deliberate partial scrolling uses a cap and shoulder to finish the visible boundary.
- **Palette scope:** theme-level inactive colors also affect classic tabs. Quiet Light uses a `#E4E4E4` strip against the `#F5F5F5` document, `#54494B` inactive/modern-hover text, and `#765500` warning text. Its warning color applies theme-wide, not only to tabs.

## Accessibility and consistency

| Area | Validation / consideration |
| --- | --- |
| Text contrast | Adjusted default-theme ordinary inactive labels pass 4.5:1 at rest and hover. Quiet Light's minimum is **4.995:1 across 21 tested filename states**, including warning decorations, hover, inactive groups, and upper-row selection. |
| Contrast exceptions | Unchanged Solarized Dark has a 4.23:1 resting sample; Solarized Light has 3.57:1 resting / 3.84:1 hover samples. Custom themes and every decoration color are not covered by these results. |
| Keyboard and accessible names | Tests preserve the complete filename in ARIA labels and reveal inactive close actions on keyboard focus. Automatic reveal retains focus-ring clearance at the viewport edge. |
| High contrast | Dark/Light HC checks cover one connected well outline, active/inactive groups, solid multi-selection versus dashed keyboard focus, and no geometry shift. Single/hidden-tab modes retain their editor-card frame. |
| Responsive layout | Tests cover equal row heights, selected fill on every row, hover-stable corners, filename/badge/action space, icon collapse and recovery, fractional-width reveal, and selection after closing scrolled tabs. |
| Style boundaries | Tests cover connected-mode gating, Pill colors, and explicit foreground customizations. Agents-window pill tabs remain unchanged. |

These are targeted automated and visual checks, not an end-to-end screen-reader audit or comprehensive WCAG certification.

## Enable

```jsonc
{
  "workbench.experimental.modernUI": true,
  "workbench.experimental.modernUIEditorTabStyle": "connected"
}
```

Use `workbench.editor.wrapTabs` for multiple rows and `workbench.editor.tabSizing: "shrink"` for constrained widths. Set the tab style to `"pill"` to compare. The tab-style setting requires Modern UI to be enabled.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path and forced-layout mechanism are explicit: `EditorGroupView.layout` calls the tab control on each group resize, the control schedules at most once per animation frame, and the new class controls `display` of tab children. Removing that class, reading `offsetWidth`, restoring it, and then entering existing geometry-reading layout code guarantees repeated style/layout work for narrow tabs. Exact milliseconds vary by tab count and platform, which affects severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: browser style recalculation and DOM layout for tab icon, description, and width geometry
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows linearly with the number of open tabs in each laid-out editor group and repeats once per animation frame during window or sash resizing; narrow tabs incur the geometry-changing remove/re-add cycle every frame.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked UI-frame work and dropped frames during continuous resize/layout
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, the tab layout path did not clear and restore a geometry-affecting class across every tab or perform these added per-tab computed-style/text measurements before the existing wrapping measurements.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every connected-tab layout now expands all narrow tabs, performs per-tab computed-style/text work, forces geometry measurement, and collapses the tabs again before the existing wrapping/non-wrapping measurements run.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 2099 newly removes `connected-tab-narrow` from every tab on every `doLayoutTabs` pass. The added CSS at connectedEditorTabs.css:335-338 makes that class hide icon and description elements with `display: none`, so removing it changes tab geometry. The same new method then reads every `tab.offsetWidth` at line 2134 and re-adds the class, before `doLayoutTabsWrapping` performs further offset/scroll measurements.
Findings.Title: Avoid expanding every narrow tab during each layout
Findings.Impact: Dragging an editor-group sash or resizing a window with connected Modern UI and many compressed tabs can miss frames and feel visibly janky because the tab strip performs two geometry states and collection-wide DOM measurements each frame.
Findings.Evidence: `EditorGroupView.layout` calls `titleControl.layout` for every editor-group resize; `MultiEditorTabsControl.layout` runs the work on the next animation frame. In the new `layoutConnectedTabLabels`, line 2099 removes `connected-tab-narrow` from all tabs; connectedEditorTabs.css:335-338 uses that class to set the icon and description to `display: none`. Line 2134 then reads `offsetWidth` for all tabs, forcing layout with those elements restored, and the following loop restores the class. `doLayoutTabsWrapping` immediately reads `offsetWidth`, `scrollWidth`, and potentially `offsetHeight` again, requiring the browser to resolve the second geometry state. The canvas LRU only caches text widths and does not avoid these DOM passes.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep each tab's intrinsic minimum-width measurement cached and invalidate it only when its label, decoration, font/theme, or relevant options change. On pure container resizes, preserve the current narrow class and only update tabs whose narrow state actually changes, avoiding the expand-measure-collapse cycle before the existing layout pass.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize a window or drag an editor-group sash with connected Modern UI tabs, especially when tabs are compressed.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `EditorGroupView.layout` synchronously enters title/tab layout; `MultiEditorTabsControl` coalesces it to the next animation frame, but the full per-tab measurement must finish within that frame before the resized editor UI settles.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Open tabs per editor group, number of visible editor groups, and resize/sash-drag animation frames; realistic pressure cases in the added tests use ten tabs, while real sessions can have many more.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One tab-layout task per control per animation frame; editor groups are laid out by the workbench layout flow, with no worker offload or additional backpressure beyond animation-frame coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Canvas text widths use a 256-entry LRU keyed by font, letter spacing, and text, so warm layouts avoid repeated `measureText` calls. The cache does not cover per-tab `getComputedStyle`, geometry-changing class resets, CSS custom-property writes, or `offsetWidth`/`offsetTop` reads, so the reported browser work repeats on warm layouts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed class directly controls `display`, it is removed before an `offsetWidth` read and restored before existing geometry reads, and the resize call path is explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame cost depends on platform, zoom, theme CSS complexity, number of groups, and open-tab count; the repeated two-state layout mechanism is definite, while whether a given machine drops frames is workload-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: the diff adds collection-wide style/geometry work and a repeated expand-measure-collapse cycle on every frame-coalesced layout.

Scenarios.Scenario: Horizontally scroll a tab strip while the active connected tab is partly clipped.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The scroll listener synchronously updates clipping classes before the tab-strip visual state is painted; it performs arithmetic and class toggles without geometry reads.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scroll-event frequency; work is constant per event and independent of total tab count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous callback per delivered scroll event; browser event coalescing applies, with no explicit additional throttler.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Stored connected-tab bounds are reused between scroll events until invalidated by a layout or tab-state change. Text-width caching is not involved on the scroll-only path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that scrolling reaches the new clipping updater; high that it avoids DOM geometry reads after bounds are captured.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Paint cost from the clipping masks varies by browser/GPU, but the JavaScript path is constant-cardinality and no forced-layout mechanism was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the new per-scroll work is bounded to one active tab and one overflow edge, with no synchronous layout read.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle Modern UI density, enablement, or connected-versus-pill tab style across main and auxiliary windows.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A relevant configuration event updates classes, then synchronously invokes main workbench layout and each auxiliary window layout before the setting change is visually complete.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of open auxiliary windows per settings change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Layouts are invoked serially: main layout first, then one call per auxiliary window.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration values are read directly; class state is updated on every registered container. No cache or coalescing is used, but changes are user-driven and infrequent.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the synchronous all-window layout path; low concern because cardinality and frequency are bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users typically have few auxiliary windows and rarely toggle these settings; no realistic high-frequency trigger was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: explicit relayout is required for changed metrics and occurs only on infrequent configuration changes with small window cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or activate editors, or update dirty, selection, capability, and label state in a connected tab group.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening, activating, relabeling, dirtying, or changing capabilities redraws affected tabs and schedules tab layout before the updated strip geometry is finalized.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of tabs in the affected group and frequency of coalesced editor state changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Multiple requests in one frame are coalesced by the existing animation-frame layout scheduler; label events also use an existing zero-delay `RunOnceScheduler`.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tab text widths can be reused by the LRU after first layout, but label changes can add new keys. The LRU bounds retention at 256 entries; connected geometry is cleared and recomputed after dirty/capability/selection updates.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed invalidation methods and existing editor-group event forwarding directly reach the new layout path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Event frequency depends on extensions, autosave, and editor type; coalescing limits bursts, but each resulting layout still pays the reported collection-wide measurement cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the reported repeated layout issue; no separate finding because these events trigger the same mechanism rather than an independent regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load or switch a built-in theme while connected tabs are enabled.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Applying a theme regenerates CSS variables/rules through existing theming participants; the added participant emits one rule and does not block on I/O.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Theme switches and DOM size; switches are infrequent and added JavaScript work is constant.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Theme application follows the existing serialized theme update path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Theme JSON is loaded through existing built-in theme mechanisms; the changed rspack matcher alters packaging coverage but introduces no new runtime fetch or per-item loading loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation was added to runtime theme application.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Style recalculation size depends on DOM size, but the diff adds only one generated rule plus static CSS selectors and no scaling runtime traversal of its own.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: color changes and one theming rule do not establish a new scaling or boundary cost beyond normal theme restyling.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 31 changed files and all paginated large patches. One medium-confidence-in-magnitude, high-confidence-in-mechanism layout regression was reported: connected tab layout repeatedly expands, measures, and collapses every narrow tab on each animation-frame layout. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary was introduced on the reviewed product paths; caches, scroll work, auxiliary-window relayout, and lifecycle retention were also checked.
